messages.content: Write the opening pitch section of a README for a new open source charting library. Around 200 words.

output:
Names and numbers below are invented placeholders — swap in your real bundle size, marks, and license before shipping.

---

# Strata

You know the shape of the problem. The stock bar chart looks fine until a designer asks for a dotted median line, and suddenly you're four levels deep in `plugins.annotation.line1.scaleID`, reading GitHub issues from 2019.

Strata is a rendering layer, not a chart menu. You get scales, axes, and five marks — `bar`, `line`, `area`, `point`, `rule` — and you compose them yourself. A candlestick is a `rule` behind a `bar`. Nobody had to ship a `candlestick` type.

The core is 14 kB gzipped, no dependencies. It renders to SVG on the server and hydrates only the marks you made interactive, so a static report ships zero JS.

Data goes in as plain arrays or an Arrow table. Colors are yours: we include one neutral palette that holds 3:1 contrast in light and dark, and no brand blue.

It is not a dashboard framework. There's no theme marketplace, no `<Dashboard>`, no telemetry. Animation stops at scale transitions — past that, bring your own.

MIT licensed. React and Svelte bindings live in this repo.

---

Two notes on the draft. The opening leads with a failure you've had rather than a claim about the library, which is the part most README pitches skip. And the "it is not" paragraph does real work: saying what you refuse to build is the fastest way to tell someone whether to keep reading.
